beats.narration_text: Three beats, in order. One: VERDICT recap — ClaudeVerdictArtifact, Liam-narrated, with a half-second lead pause and a handoff line. Two: YOUR TURN — ClaudeComposerAsk with a relevant prompt the viewer can run, greeting: Your turn. Three: TITLE re-read — ClaudeTitleOutro, Liam re-reads the title as the sign-off.

whatItDoes: Standardize the closing 3 beats of any claude-explainer reel
Beat 1: VERDICT recap (ClaudeVerdictArtifact) with 0.5s lead + handoff line
Beat 2: YOUR TURN (ClaudeComposerAsk) — relevant per-reel prompt, Liam reads it
Beat 3: TITLE re-read (ClaudeTitleOutro) — Liam re-reads the title
phaseGates: Draft: LLM drafts YOUR TURN prompts + recaps → drafts.json
Human review: gate on drafts.json + report before any audio spend
Apply: transformer edits closing 3 beats in place (idempotent)
Re-render: art run <reel> → then human decides re-upload

beats.narration_text: Five steps. Draft: LLM drafts the YOUR TURN prompts per slug from the reel's own material. Dry-run: see planned edits without writing anything. Human review: gate on drafts.json — the one non-deterministic step needs sign-off. Apply: transformer edits the closing three beats idempotently. Re-render: art run, then human decides re-upload.

The draft shows the YOUR TURN prompt drawn from the scout reel's material: a question a student would paste into Claude after watching. The transformer adds the YOUR TURN beat and TITLE re-read beat. The human reviews the drafts.json before approving audio spend.

beats.narration_text: Law one: every claude-explainer reel should end the same way — Liam hands off from the body, recaps on the artifact card, gives the viewer a prompt to run, and re-reads the title. The uniformity is a user experience guarantee. The viewer always knows what's coming: recap, try it, title. No endings that fade out on nothing.

props.quote: Every claude-explainer reel should end the same way: Liam hands off from the body, recaps on the artifact card, gives the viewer a prompt to run, and re-reads the title.
mechanismLines: Three-beat structure: VERDICT → YOUR TURN → TITLE
Handoff wording: 'Thanks Bear' if Bear body; 'Let's recap' if Liam body
0.5s lead silence on VERDICT — pause before the recap
Uniformity = UX guarantee for the viewer

beats.narration_text: Law two: the prompt must be relevant to the video, so it is drafted per reel — never templated. A generic 'try this yourself' prompt is not a YOUR TURN prompt. The prompt is drawn from the reel's material: the mechanism it explained, the artifact it produced. A curious viewer should want to paste it into Claude the moment the video ends.

props.quote: The prompt must be RELEVANT to the video, so it is drafted per reel, never templated.
props.source: skills/make/your-turn/SKILL.md — Auto-drafting the YOUR TURN prompt
mechanismLines: Prompt drawn from reel's material: mechanism + artifact
First person, 3–5 sentences, ending in a concrete multi-part ask
Grounded in the same mechanism as the video — one step deeper
Templated prompts are rejected; LLM drafts per slug from narration_text

beats.narration_text: Law three: audio-first — the handoff, the read prompt, and the title re-read are new Liam lines: regenerate audio, then conform. Never hand-time. The transformer edits the beat sheet; audio gen runs after human approval. The idempotent contract means re-running the transformer on an already-updated sheet adds nothing and stacks nothing.
